motion_provenance.what: hip hinge with a neutral spine, soft knees (~5 deg top, ~18 deg bottom), trunk ~80 deg at the bottom, weights close to the legs
motion_provenance.source: ExRx 'Dumbbell Straight-leg Deadlift'; NSCA Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning 4th ed.; McGill, Low Back Disorders

motion_provenance.what: balance: whole-body centre of mass over the mid-foot (segment masses and centres)
motion_provenance.source: Winter 2009, Biomechanics and Motor Control of Human Movement, table 4.1

motion_provenance.what: muscles: hamstrings primary; gluteus maximus, erector spinae (keeps the back flat) secondary
motion_provenance.source: free-exercise-db 'Stiff-Legged Dumbbell Deadlift' (Unlicense, used by the app library); ExRx

motion_provenance.what: muscle roles (target -> primary, synergists -> secondary, stabilizers -> stabilizing)

start_position: Stand tall, dumbbells in front of the thighs
eccentric: Push the hips back, slide the weights down the legs
bottom_hold: Feel the stretch in the back of the thighs
concentric: Drive the hips forward to stand up
Squeeze the glutes at the top

validation_profile.comment: Thresholds for automated checks. They catch defects in the animation data (jumps, slides, penetration, asymmetry). They do not certify exercise technique; that needs a qualified human.
validation_profile.max_hand_into_bar_comment: The skin of the palm is rigid in this rig. Up to 8 mm of palm pad inside the bar stands for soft tissue pressed flat by the load; more than that, or any finger passing through the bar, is a defect.

technical_cues: Back flat from head to hips
Weights stay close to the legs
common_mistakes: Bending the knees into a squat
Letting the weights drift away from the legs
muscle_roles_note: Three levels (Kiệt 15/11): primary = carries the load and produces the main force; secondary = directly assists the movement; stabilizing = holds posture and keeps joints stable. With nearly straight knees hip extension is mostly the hamstrings' (ExRx target); gluteus maximus and adductor magnus assist. Erector spinae keeps the back flat, upper trapezius and rhomboids hold the shoulders against the hanging weight, forearm flexors the grip.
